You see a bare back. Do not lend money or hand out advice right now: it may turn against you. Someone turns their back and walks away — envy and jealousy are working against you. Seeing your own back — save your strength and look after your health.

You see a beard. Someone you dislike will push their will on you, and the struggle may cost you money. A grey beard — bad luck and quarrels. Someone pulls your beard — your property is at risk. Combing and admiring your beard — success may go to your head; stay humble.

You see a swollen belly. Take care of your health and do not overstrain yourself. Something moving on your belly means humiliation and hard work. A healthy belly points to strong, sometimes reckless desires.
You put on a new fashionable belt. You will soon make a deal with a stranger, and it may hurt your income. An old, outdated belt means you will rightly be blamed for rudeness: watch your words.
Something bites you. You will regret something done that cannot be undone. Beware of an ill-wisher: losses may come through them.

You see your own brain. Unfriendly surroundings are irritating you and souring your mood; look for a place where you feel at ease. Seeing an animal's brain means inner worries. Eating brains means new knowledge and unexpected profit.

You burn your hand on a clear fire. Good news: your intentions are pure, and friends will support you. Burning your feet walking over coals means you can do what others think impossible. If the fire overcomes you, beware of betrayal by false friends.

You see a new coat. A new coat means recognition and honour for your work. Wearing someone else's coat — you will have to ask a friend to vouch for you. A torn coat — a close friendship cools and work turns dull. Losing your coat — overconfidence will cost you dearly.

You have a nagging cough. Look after your health: with sensible habits you will soon get your strength back. Hearing others cough — you will find yourself in unpleasant surroundings, but you'll get out of them in the end.
You have a cut. Poor health or a friend's dishonesty will spoil your good mood. Look after your health and do not rush to trust people who have only just come close.

You see happy, bright faces around you. A good dream: joy and good luck lie ahead. Ugly or frowning faces mean trouble. A strange, eerie face means enemies and misfortune around you. Your own face in a mirror means dissatisfaction with yourself over unfulfilled plans. Your beloved's face looking old means a separation.
You fall and are badly frightened. A great struggle lies ahead, but in the end you will reach honour and wealth. If you are hurt in the fall, expect hardship and friends drifting away.

You have a fever. You are fretting over trifles while the best of life slips by; pull yourself together and do something worthwhile. Seeing your relatives with a fever means small cares for your loved ones; surround them with kindness.

You see a fine, smooth forehead. People will value your good judgement and fairness. An ugly forehead: annoyances in private matters. Stroking your child's forehead: friends will sincerely praise your children.

You put on a new hat. A profitable change of place or job lies ahead. For a woman, a beautiful new hat means wealth and admiration. Losing your hat: setbacks at work and broken appointments. The wind blowing your hat off: sudden changes, not all of them welcome.

You see someone's head. You will meet influential people who will help you with an important matter. Your own head: look after your nerves and rest. A headache: worries ahead. Having two heads: a fast but shaky rise. Washing your head: respected people will come to you for advice.

Your heart aches. Trouble is brewing at work because of your own mistake. Find it and fix it in time. Seeing your own heart: save your strength and look after your health. An animal's heart: you will beat your rivals and earn respect. Eating a chicken heart: an unusual wish will lead you down a hard but rewarding path.

You jump over an obstacle. Everything you take on will work out. Jumping and falling back: annoying troubles, so be patient. Jumping down from a wall: do not gamble money blindly and do not rush in love.

Your knees ache and will not bend. Some trouble may be ahead. Be more careful in your affairs and look after your health. Knees that are too big: sudden bad luck. A woman seeing she has pretty, smooth knees: many admirers, but serious intentions will take a while.
You walk with a limp. A small, unexpected worry will spoil your mood. Seeing someone else limp means a friend's behavior will hurt your feelings. The dream points to small setbacks, not big trouble.

You have a mustache in the dream. Pride and pushiness may harm you, so be more modest. For a woman, admiring a mustache warns of temptation: be careful. For a man, shaving off his mustache means he will break with bad company and win back his good name.

You look at your own neck. Family worries may get in the way of your work. Admiring someone else's neck means chasing appearances could upset things at home. For a woman, seeing her neck thick warns her to watch her temper.

You have a nightmare and can't shake it off. Arguments and setbacks at work are possible, so stay out of needless conflicts. The dream also advises you to look after your health and watch what you eat. For a young woman, it foretells disappointment and undeserved slights.

You look at your own nose. You have a strong character and can carry any task through. If your nose looks smaller than usual, things may not go well. Hair on your nose means you will take on something unusual and pull it off through sheer will. A nosebleed warns of serious trouble: be careful.
You take pills. New responsibilities will come, and they will bring you satisfaction and joy. Giving pills to others — you will be criticized for being hard to deal with; be gentler.

You have pimples on your skin. Small worries will bother you. Others with pimples — complaints and fuss from other people. Pimples spoiling your looks — acquaintances will gossip about your behavior. These are only small annoyances; do not take them to heart.

You see bright ribbons. Cheerful, pleasant people will be around you, and everyday worries will not weigh on you much. For a young woman, decking herself with ribbons foretells a proposal soon, if she avoids being careless. Seeing other girls in ribbons means rivalry. Buying ribbons means an easy, pleasant life.
You are putting on a shirt. Being unfaithful could push the one you love away. Losing your shirt: trouble at work or in love. A torn shirt: bad luck. A dirty shirt: take care of your health.

You see a skeleton. Look after your health and beware of enemies: misunderstandings and hurt are possible. You are a skeleton yourself: you wear yourself out with needless worry; be gentler with yourself. A skeleton haunting you: a sudden shock or money trouble.

You see grinning skulls. Quarrels at home and a slowdown at work are possible. Seeing a friend's skull: someone will harm you out of envy. Seeing your own skull: you will blame yourself for the past; let it go.

You get a splinter. Small annoyances from relatives or jealous rivals lie ahead. A splinter in your foot while visiting means an unpleasant visit. Don't neglect small tasks or they will slowly go wrong.

You see a stain on your clothes. Trouble over small things is coming. Don't blow it out of proportion. A stain on your hands means the same small worries. A stain on someone else's clothes or skin means someone may let you down.

You are struggling with someone. Serious difficulties are coming, but if you win in the dream, you will overcome them in life. Losing the struggle means you should gather strength before making your move.

You see a tattoo on your body. Circumstances may take you away from home for a long time. Tattoos on others mean someone's unusual feelings will make you the object of jealousy. Being a tattoo artist means a passion for something new may distance you from friends.
You see a graceful throat. A promotion and a rise in status await you. A sore throat means you'll be disappointed in a friend and worry about it.

You see a thumb. Cunning people will be around you, and luck will be fickle. Be careful. A sore thumb means losses and unpleasant company. A missing thumb means loneliness. A very large thumb means quick, brilliant success.

You see your own tongue. Acquaintances may frown on you. Be more careful with your words. Seeing someone else's tongue means gossip about you. Something wrong with your tongue means careless talk will get you into trouble.

You see someone in uniform. Influential friends will help you get what you want. A young woman wearing a uniform will find love that is returned. People in strange uniforms point to a falling-out between families or friends. A loved one looking sad in uniform means a long time apart.

You wear a veil. You are not fully honest with the one you love, and that may lead to games and tricks. Others in veils point to slander from false friends. An old or torn veil warns of deceit around you. A bridal veil means a happy change. Throwing a veil aside points to a break-up.

You are wounded. Distress and an unlucky turn in your affairs lie ahead. Seeing others wounded means friends may treat you unfairly. Dressing a wound means you will have reason to be glad of your good luck.

Your arm or leg is cut off. You may lose something at work: a minor position or part of your income. Losing a whole arm or leg — a slump in your affairs. For a sailor — a storm. A severed arm — discord between partners; watch out for deceit.
You see your arm. If the arm is hurt or cut off — discord between partners; watch out for deceit. Look after your relationship: talk openly about what bothers you before it grows.

You see someone's eye. Ill-wishers are watching you closely, waiting for a chance to do harm. For someone in love, the dream says to stay alert: a rival may be close. Brown eyes mean cunning, blue eyes indecision, grey eyes a love of flattery. Sore eyes mean trouble.

You itch all over. Unpleasant chores will come your way. Seeing people with an itch and avoiding them: your fears are groundless, and your efforts will succeed. Having a rash yourself: you will be treated harshly, but do not shift the blame onto others.

You are angry and shouting. A hard trial and a disappointment in someone close are ahead. Friends or family are angry at you while you stay calm — you will reconcile the quarrelling sides and earn their gratitude.

You feel strong anxiety. Sometimes this is a good sign: after a hard time, success and fresh energy will come. If you are anxious about something very important — be careful; complications are possible both at work and in your relationships.

You see a bald man. Smooth operators will try a deal against you, but if you stay alert you will outsmart them. A bald baby — a happy home, a loving partner and good children. For a young woman, a bald man — think hard about the next marriage proposal. A bare, bald hill — hard times.

You wander barefoot at night in torn clothes. Your hopes may not come true, and things will be an uphill struggle. Do not give up: the hard stretch will pass if you save your strength and do not rush.

You see yourself grown stout. Growing wealth and a comfortable home await you. Seeing others plump — busy, prosperous times. Seeing yourself grossly fat — take a look at your habits and actions. A distorted reflection, as in a funhouse mirror — trouble.

You find yourself naked. Beware of gossip and rash promises. Seeing others naked means someone will try to lead you off the right path. Suddenly noticing you are naked and covering up means you want to give up something that doesn't suit you. Swimming naked in clear water promises many admirers.

You see yourself as ugly. There will be friction with someone you love, and your plans will lose their shine for a while. For a young woman who feels ugly in the dream, it is a hint to be gentler with her partner, or the relationship may crack.

You have gone blind. A sharp turn in your affairs is coming: protect what you have and avoid extra spending. Seeing a blind person means someone worthy will ask you for help; do not refuse. A blindfold means someone may deceive you, so check everything yourself.

You see blood. Be careful: ill-wishers may try to block your success. Bloodstained clothes warn you against dubious new friendships. Blood flowing from a wound means tiredness and worry; save your strength. Blood on your hands means bad luck unless you take care of yourself and your affairs. Bleeding heavily means gossip about you.
You see a pile of bones. Bad influences and shortage surround you: keep away from doubtful people. Your own bones sticking out mean someone is scheming against you; stay alert.

You put on new boots. Luck in your affairs and a rise in income. Your boots on someone else mean a rival may take your place in your beloved's heart. Old, torn boots mean look after your health and steer clear of traps.

You climb a mountain. If you reach the top, you will overcome the toughest obstacles on your way to success. Failing to reach the top — your plans will need to change. Climbing a ladder to the last rung — success at work; a ladder breaking — sudden difficulties. Climbing up a house wall when a window opens to let you in — a bold plan will succeed even though friends disapprove.

You see clean new clothes. Clean new clothes promise prosperity and well-being. Dirty and torn clothes — someone is trying to deceive you; don't trust strangers. A huge pile of clothes — don't overspend, or you'll run short of what you really need.
You are freezing. Keep a close eye on your affairs: ill-wishers are trying to harm you. Look after your health: dress warmly and don't overwork.
You comb your hair. A friendship may cool, and some of your belongings may go missing. Look after your relationships and check in on your loved ones more often.

You crawl along the ground. You may be given a humiliating task. Crawling over stones — you have missed your chances. Crawling through mud with others — a slump at work and reproach from friends. For a young woman, the dream advises minding her conduct so as not to lose her sweetheart's respect.

You hear cries for help. Serious trouble lies ahead, but if you stay alert you will get through it and even come out ahead. A cry of surprise — help will come from where you least expect it. The roar of wild animals — stay alert and take no needless risks. Relatives or friends calling for help — they are struggling right now; support them.
You walk on crutches. You will have to rely heavily on other people's help. Seeing others on crutches — your work will bring less than you hoped.

You are crying. Expect worrying news and unrest in the family. Others crying means a happy reunion after a long rift. For a young woman, the dream points to a quarrel with her partner that her willingness to give in will settle.
You feel dizzy. Peace at home may be shaken, and your affairs will look gloomy for a while. Do not rush decisions until you feel solid ground under your feet again.
You see earrings. Good news and interesting work ahead. Broken earrings mean nasty gossip will be spread about you.
You see someone's ears. Someone ill-meaning is listening to your words to use them against you. Watch what you say and to whom, especially about other people's business.
You faint. Worrying news about your family and about people far away. For a young woman, the dream advises looking after her health and living a steadier life.
You feel very tired. Look after your strength: work may weigh on you, and your health needs rest. Seeing others exhausted means your energy will come back slowly; don't rush yourself.

You feel afraid in your dream. Your coming plans may not turn out as well as you hope. If the fright is brief and passes quickly, it means small worries that will soon be forgotten. For a young woman, it warns of disappointment in love.

You look at your own feet. Someone with a strong will may try to bend you to theirs; stand your ground. Seeing other people's feet means you will defend your rights gently but firmly. Washing your feet: others may take advantage of you. Aching feet: awkward family quarrels.
You see well-kept fingernails. Well-kept nails point to a love of learning and a careful way with money. Dirty nails warn of family trouble caused by the wild antics of the young.

You see beautiful clean fingers. Your love will be returned, and your kindness will earn you a good name. Dirty or scratched, bleeding fingers mean hardships and low spirits. Fingers cut off warn that ill-wishers may take part of your income or inheritance.

You are flying in your dream. Flying on white wings above green trees means success in work and love. Seeing the sun while flying: your worries are needless, things will work out. Flying low over the ground: a little tiredness that will soon pass. Flying over muddy water: keep your affairs private. Falling while flying: a setback, but if you wake as you fall, you'll rise again.
You see freckles on your face. Small annoying incidents may spoil your happiness. Looking at your freckles in a mirror: you risk losing your partner to a rival; give them more attention.

You are dressed in fur. Want and hardship will pass you by. Seeing fine fur: honour and wealth. Trading in furs: prosperity and many interesting ventures. For a young woman, wearing luxurious fur means marrying a wise person.

You see a pair of glasses. Strangers will step into your affairs and change something in them. Don't take the word of people who promise too much. Broken glasses mean a falling-out with someone close over dubious pleasures.

You put on new gloves. You'll be careful and thrifty but not stingy; disputes at work will be settled in your favour. Old or torn gloves: deceit and losses. Losing your gloves: you'll have to rely on yourself alone. Finding a pair of gloves: a new romance.

You see thick, well-groomed hair. Neat, nicely styled hair means your affairs will improve. Soft hair growing thick: happiness and comfort. Tangled, uncombed hair: burdens at work and in relationships. Having your hair cut: disappointments. Snow-white hair: a long and fortunate life. Flowers in your hair: coming troubles will prove less frightening than they look.

You see beautiful hands. Recognition and quick progress in your field lie ahead. Washing your hands: a joyful celebration. Seeing your hands grown large: quick advancement. Blood on your hands: a falling-out with relatives. Tied hands: difficulties; untying them, you'll gain the upper hand. Holding fire without getting burned: a high position.
You are hungry. Home may lack warmth and comfort. Lovers should not rush into marriage. Think about what you are really missing, and look after yourself and your loved ones.

You laugh and feel cheerful. Your plans will succeed, and you will have bright company. Hearing children laugh happily means joy and good health. Laughing wildly at something strange means discord around you. Laughing at someone's misfortune warns you not to hurt friends for your own gain. Hearing mocking laughter means setbacks and feeling unwell.

You feel too lazy to do anything. You may make a mistake when starting something new and feel bitterly let down. For a young woman who sees her partner as lazy, the dream advises warmth: coldness drives serious people away.

You see your own legs, strong and well shaped. A happy future and devoted friends await you. Admiring someone's beautiful legs warns you not to lose your head over a crush. A wounded leg means losses. A wooden leg warns you not to pretend in front of friends. Three or more legs mean more plans than real gain. Being unable to walk means tight money.

You see full, beautiful lips. Harmony and comfort lie ahead, and in love, affection that is returned and faithful. Thick, unattractive lips mean unpleasant encounters, hasty decisions and short tempers. Thin lips mean you will master the most complex matters. Sore or swollen lips mean hardship and unwise cravings.
You are lucky in everything. Your wishes will come true, and pleasant tasks lie ahead. To someone who has lost heart, this dream promises a lift and a return of prosperity.

You dream that you are going mad. Hard times are ahead: look after your health so you don't lose what you have built. Seeing others go mad means fickle friends and dashed hopes. For a young woman, the dream advises not rushing her choice of partner.

You take medicine. If it tastes pleasant, trouble will come but soon turn out for your good. Bitter, nasty medicine means a long stretch of sorrows, so look after your health. Giving medicine to others warns you not to abuse someone's trust.

You see yourself grown old. Something you have started may fail; do not rush and check your plans. Arguing about your age — your stubbornness will anger your family. For a young woman, seeing her beloved grown old — look after the relationship; it can be lost through neglect.
You are in pain. Don't torture yourself with regrets over small things: they aren't worth it. Seeing others in pain means you are making a mistake somewhere, so review your actions.

You breathe in perfume. Happy events are on their way. Putting on perfume — you will seek admiration and get it. A scent so strong it makes you dizzy — do not lose your head in joy. Spilling perfume — you will lose something that gives you pleasure. Breaking a bottle — a cherished wish may fall apart at the last moment. Perfume as a gift — exciting but risky pleasures.

You see yourself pregnant. The dream warns of discontent and tension in your relationship. If you really are expecting — an easy birth and a quick recovery. For a single young woman — beware of gossip and hardship.

You are running with others. A celebration is coming, and your affairs will move toward success. Running alone: you will outpace everyone in wealth and standing. Stumbling or falling: guard your property and reputation. Running from danger: a risk of losses and worry.
You feel gloomy and sad. Something that seemed promising may let you down. Seeing others sad means unpleasant interruptions in your affairs. For lovers, the dream foretells a rift.

You are shaving. You will run your own affairs and household, even if there are some arguments. Someone else shaves you: do not let yourself be fooled. A smooth face afterwards: calm days. A dull razor pulling your skin: give people no reason to gossip. Only thinking about a shave: good plans, but not enough drive.

You put on new shoes. Changes will work in your favor. Polishing shoes: your affairs will improve, with good reason to rejoice. Shabby, dirty shoes: harsh criticism will make you enemies. Shoes that pinch: someone will make fun of you. Untied laces: quarrels and losses. Losing your shoes: a breakup.
You see bare shoulders. Happy changes will make you see the world in a new light. Your own shoulders look thin: you depend too much on other people's whims; find your own joy.

You are ill. This dream tells you to pay more attention to yourself and save your strength. Someone in your family is ill: unexpected worry at home; be patient with one another. Seeing sickness all around: discord may creep into the home.

You are dressed in silk. Your high hopes will be fulfilled, and people who fell out will make peace. For a young woman, old silk: pride in her family roots and the attention of a wealthy, older admirer. Dirty or torn silk: guard your good name.
You spit. Something that started well may end in disappointment. Don't celebrate too soon. Someone spitting on you means a quarrel and cooling feelings.

You stumble. Obstacles will rise on your path to success, but you'll get past them as long as you don't fall. Tumbling off something means you should be more focused and stop putting things off. Seeing others tumble means you'll gain from their carelessness.
You are suffocating. Something a loved one does may hurt you deeply. Don't keep the hurt inside. After this dream, take care of your health and don't overload yourself.
You are covered in sweat. You will come out of a much-gossiped-about difficulty with new respect. Do not fear the talk: the trouble that weighs on you now will turn into honor.
You are crying. Sadness may wash over you for a while. Let yourself feel it and it will ease. Seeing others in tears means your sorrow will touch those close to you; share it rather than hide it.

Your teeth are falling out. This warns of unpleasant news and hardships. Look after your health and keep an eye on your affairs. Loose teeth mean setbacks and gloomy news. Getting fillings means you'll recover something lost. Admiring your white, beautiful teeth means happiness and wishes come true. Being toothless means it's hard to move ahead, so take care of yourself; others without teeth mean enemies are slandering you in vain.
You feel terror. Disappointment and loss may lie ahead. Stay calm. Seeing others in terror means friends' troubles will hit you hard.

You are thirsty. You are reaching for things that are still beyond you. Don't give up. Quenching your thirst with a pleasant drink means your wishes will come true. Seeing others drink means influential people will help you.
You see a pair of trousers. You may be tempted to do something dishonest. Don't give in. Putting them on inside out means some passion is taking a stronger hold on you.
You are undressing. Beware of gossip: unpleasant rumours about you may spread. Seeing others undressed points to forbidden pleasures that will later bring regret.
You see urine. Tiredness may make you irritable with friends; give yourself a rest. Urinating in the dream points to bad luck and a trying time in love.

You are vomiting. Look after your health and keep away from scandals. Seeing others vomit means you will see through people who want your help under false pretences. Vomiting blood points to tiredness and household worries; save your strength and do not overload yourself.

You dream that you have woken up. Strange events will darken your mood for a while. Walking through green fields and feeling that you are waking — bright times lie ahead, though there will be letdowns along the way.

You walk through beautiful places. Good luck and the goodwill of others await you. Walking through thorny undergrowth points to tangled affairs and coolness from loved ones. Walking at night means setbacks and a long search for peace. For a young woman, walking quickly brings something she longs for.

You have warts. It will be hard to defend your good name against attacks. Warts leaving your hands mean you will overcome obstacles on the way to prosperity. Warts on others point to ill-wishers nearby. Treating warts means you will vigorously ward off a threat to yourself and your loved ones.
You are washing yourself. You are too proud of your romances, and that may lead to gossip. Keep private matters private and do not boast about your conquests.
You have wings. You will worry about someone close who has gone far away. Seeing the wings of birds means you will overcome hardship and gain wealth and honour.
You are yawning. You will look for peace and energy but will not find them right away. Others yawning means one of your friends is having a hard time and will need your support.

You feast at a rich table. A good dream: friends will gladly come to your aid. Well-dressed guests, fine dishes and old wine — great success in everything and joy among friends. Empty tables or strange, unpleasant faces — misunderstandings and disappointments.
You walk into a bar. Life around you will get busy, and luck may come quickly. Working behind the bar yourself — do not chase your goal by shady means.

You see a cabbage. A poor sign: disorder may creep into your affairs and relationships. Green cabbage means unfaithfulness in love. Cutting heads of cabbage means you are bringing trouble on yourself by overspending.
You drink a cocktail. You will show your loved ones one face while secretly chasing wild fun. Don't lead a double life: the pretence will come out and damage trust.
You see coconuts. Your hopes may fall through: sly rivals are posing as eager friends. Dead coconut palms — losses and sorrow. Check who is really on your side.
You see cucumbers. A good dream: health, prosperity and plenty. If you are ill and serve cucumbers, you will soon recover. For married people the dream brings a pleasant change.

You are one of many guests at a dinner. Warm hospitality and pleasant attention from kind people await you. Dining alone means you will have to think hard about the basics of life. For a young woman, dinner with her beloved warns of a quarrel, unless it goes in perfect harmony; then it means joy.
You are eating jam. Pleasant surprises and trips are waiting for you. Making jam: a happy home and grateful friends.

You see lobsters. Great favors and wealth await you. Eating lobster warns you not to get too caught up with pleasure-seekers. Lobster salad means success won't spoil your generosity. Ordering lobster means a high position with many people under you.

You see melons. Look after your health and don't rush into risky ventures. Eating melon means a hasty act will cause you worry. Melons growing on green vines mean your present troubles will turn into good luck.

You see pears. Fortune will look kinder to you than before. Eating pears — mind your strength and do not expect easy success. Picking pears — pleasant surprises soon after a disappointment. Preserving pears — you will take setbacks calmly. Baking pears — love and friendships that feel bland.

You are at a picnic. Success and real enjoyment lie ahead. For young people this dream promises pure happiness. A storm or some trouble spoils the picnic — luck in work or love will be briefly postponed.
You eat a pie. Watch those who wish you ill: they are planning to harm you. Baking pies — light flirting just for fun; do not overplay it.

You eat a pineapple. A very good dream: success will come soon. Gathering pineapples — luck in the near future. Pricking your fingers while cutting one — some hassle first, but it ends in joy and success.

You see ripe plums. Joyful occasions are coming, though they will not last long. Green plums off the tree — minor discomfort. Eating plums — light flirting and fleeting pleasures. Picking plums — you will get what you want, but it will be less solid than you thought. Finding rotten ones among the good — life is not made of pleasure alone.

You see a pomegranate. You will wisely use your talents to grow your mind rather than chase harmful pleasures. Your sweetheart gives you a pomegranate — someone’s charm will turn your head, but inner strength will keep you safe. Eating one — you will surrender to another person’s charm.

You see potatoes. This dream most often brings good things. Digging potatoes — success. Eating them — real gain. Cooking them — pleasant work. Planting them — your wishes will come true. Rotten potatoes — joy fades, a harder time lies ahead.

You see raspberries. You risk getting tangled in a messy situation, though getting out of it will be rather interesting. Eating raspberries — distress at finding yourself the subject of gossip through a chance coincidence.
You are eating a salad. Unpleasant people will be around you; take care of your health and nerves. For a young woman, making a salad means her partner will be fickle and quick to quarrel.
You are making sausages. Many of your undertakings will succeed. Eating sausages: a modest but cozy home.

You see walnuts. Many joys and favours await you. Cracking a rotten walnut means bitter disappointment in your expectations. For a young woman, walnut stains on her hands point to jealousy and regrets about the past.
You eat almonds. A good sign: wealth is coming, though a little sadness will come with it for a while. Bad almonds — a cherished wish will not come true yet; wait for new circumstances.

You are eating ice cream. The things you have started will end well. Children eating ice cream: prosperity and happiness. Sour ice cream: an unexpected snag will spoil your fun. Melted ice cream: the joy you expect will stall.

You see ripe apples on a tree. A very good dream: the time has come to make your hopes real; act boldly. Red apples among green leaves — great luck. Apples at the very top — do not aim too high. Apples on the ground — flatterers are near. Rotten apples — wasted effort.

You see apricots on a tree. The future looks rosy, but bitterness is hidden in it; do not get carried away too soon. Eating apricots — a run of troubles. Others eating them — you will not like the people around you. Another reading: you are wasting time on trifles.

You eat bacon with someone. A good sign if the company is pleasant and everything is clean: comfort and luck. Rancid bacon — annoying setbacks and careless mistakes. Curing bacon cleanly — good; in smoke and salt — trouble.
You bake bread or pies. Many household chores and a modest income lie ahead; do not carry everything alone. Look after your health and ask for help: cares are lighter when shared.

You see bananas. A dull person who does not interest you may end up by your side; do not agree to a relationship out of pity. Eating bananas — a tiring job you took on yourself. Rotten bananas — do not get drawn into an unpleasant scheme. Selling bananas — effort without profit.
You eat beans. A gloomy dream: a close friend may have a hard time; support them. Growing beans — worries about children and their health. Dried beans — disappointment in everyday affairs.

You are drinking beer in a bar. Disappointments are ahead: not everything will go as you hope. Watching others drink means a schemer may get in the way of your best hopes. If the beer is fresh and tasty and the setting pleasant, things will work out.

You are drunk. Getting drunk on strong spirits means reckless living and trouble at work. Drunk on wine, you will be lucky in business and love and feel inspired. Seeing others drunk means unhappy times for you and those around you.
You are eating blackberries. Expect losses: be more careful with money and promises. Seeing blackberries means small troubles. Picking them brings bad luck.

You share bread with others. A secure living for life. Good fresh bread within reach is a kind sign. Lots of stale or spoiled bread means hard times; be thrifty. For a woman, eating bread means her children's stubbornness will cause her a lot of fuss.

You are having breakfast with others. A good sign, especially for people who work with their minds. Fresh milk, eggs and ripe fruit on the table mean quick but happy changes. Eating breakfast alone means be careful not to fall into an ill-wisher's trap.

You are eating fresh golden butter. Good health and well-carried plans; they will bring wealth and new knowledge. Eating rancid butter means you will earn a living through hard physical work. Selling butter means a small profit.

You are eating sweet cakes. A reward for your work and a good chance for bold ventures. Pancakes mean your affections are in safe hands. For lovers, cakes promise happiness. Baking them is a weaker sign than seeing or eating them. For a young woman, seeing her own wedding cake means small disappointments.

You are eating fresh, crunchy candy. Cheerful gatherings, flirting and love. Making candy means hard work will pay off. Sour candy means annoyance over secrets kept too long. Receiving a box of chocolates means compliments and prosperity. Sending one means your proposal may be turned down.
You eat cheese. Disappointment and sadness lie ahead; don't expect much good from the coming days. Don't build high hopes right now: get through this rough patch calmly and it will pass.
You see cherries. Your kindness and generosity will make people love you. Eating cherries — you will get something you have long wanted. Green cherries — good luck is coming soon.

You hold chestnuts. You may lose something in your affairs, but you will have a pleasant, loyal life partner. Eating chestnuts — a short spell of sadness, then happiness. For a young woman, the dream promises a well-off suitor and comfort.

You see chocolate. You will be able to take generous care of those who depend on you. Chocolate sweets — pleasant company and work you enjoy. Sour chocolate — small letdowns. Drinking hot chocolate — after a short run of bad luck, prosperity will come.

You see clams. You will deal with a stubborn but honest person. Eating clams — you will share in someone else's success. For a young woman eating them with her sweetheart — he will trust her with both his heart and his wallet.

You drink coffee. Friends will disapprove of your marriage plans, and at home there may be arguments. Selling coffee — losses; buying it — your affairs stay sound. Ground coffee — you will beat your troubles. Green coffee beans — you have bold rivals, stay alert.
You cook a meal. A pleasant task will come your way, and many friends will soon visit you. If the cooking is joyless and full of irritation — expect annoying hassles.

You walk through a green cornfield heavy with ears. Wealth, a rich harvest in all your affairs and peace at home await you. Ripe corn — fame and plenty. Watching others harvest corn — you will rejoice in friends' success. Eating sweet corn — harmony among friends. Withered ears — disappointments.
You drink cream. Good luck will smile on you soon. Seeing cream served — ties with wealthy people and good income. For lovers — they will soon be together.
You are drinking merrily in a noisy crowd. Today's pleasures may later harm your good name. If you try to drink clear water but cannot, you will miss out on a pleasure someone keeps offering you.

You are eating with other people. Personal gain, a cheerful atmosphere and successful ventures. Eating alone means losses and low spirits. If your plate is taken away before you finish, people who depend on you will cause you trouble.

You find a nest full of eggs. Solid wealth and family happiness. Eating eggs means unrest at home. Fresh broken eggs mean fate is preparing generous gifts. Rotten eggs mean losses. Bird eggs promise an unexpected profit.

You see figs growing on a tree. Figs on the branches point to good health and profit. Eating figs: look after your health and don't overdo it. For a young woman, figs growing on a tree promise a good marriage to a well-off person.

You see fruit ripening among the leaves. Ripening fruit points to a prosperous future. Green, unripe fruit: hasty decisions and wasted effort. Buying or selling fruit: lots of work but little income. Eating ripe fruit: changeable luck.

You walk through a garlic patch. You will rise from hardship to wealth and recognition. Eating garlic: you'll take a sober, practical view of life. For a young woman, the dream points to a marriage of convenience rather than love.

You see lush bunches of grapes among the leaves. You'll reach a prominent position and be able to bring joy to others. Eating grapes: worries and cares. For a young woman, the dream promises her dearest wish will come true. Wondering whether the berries are poisonous: doubts about success that will gradually fade.
You see honey. Real prosperity is coming your way. Eating honey: wealth and love. For lovers: a quick and happy wedding. Strained honey: an easy life, but do not get carried away by pleasure alone.

You eat a lemon. Awkward moments and disappointment may come. Lemons on a tree among leaves mean jealousy that will prove groundless. Green lemons tell you to look after your health. Shriveled lemons mean a rift with someone you love.

You see fresh green lettuce growing. After a small embarrassment, you will get something you have long wanted. Eating lettuce means petty jealousy or a small rift. Picking it warns you not to let jealousy torment you. For a woman sowing lettuce, the dream advises looking after her health. Buying lettuce warns you not to work against yourself.

You drink hard liquor. Money may come in not quite the cleanest way, but cheerful friends will gather around you. Buying liquor warns you not to claim what isn't yours. Barrels of liquor mean prosperity, but less comfort at home. Bottles mean good fortune in very real form. Treating others means generosity even toward rivals.
You see raw meat. Setbacks and discouragement lie on the road to your goal. Seeing cooked meat means someone else may get what you are striving for. Don't give up, act more boldly.

You drink milk. Plenty, joy at home and a lucky journey await you. Lots of milk means wealth and health. Spilling milk means a small loss and brief hurt from friends. Impure milk means petty troubles. Sour milk means worry over friends' troubles. Hot milk means a struggle, but success in the end. Bathing in milk means pleasant company. This dream is especially favorable for women.

You see mushrooms. Don't rush to get rich at any cost: quick money may vanish in lawsuits and idle pleasures. Eating mushrooms warns of an embarrassing situation and a dubious affair. For a young woman, the dream advises not to chase frivolous pleasures.
You eat noodles. Don't let your cravings take over: know when to stop. The dream advises moderation in everything: food, spending and fun.
You gather nuts. Success at work and luck in love await you. Eating nuts means prosperity will help you get what you want. For a woman, the dream promises great happiness.

You pick olives with cheerful friends. Your affairs will turn out well, and pleasant surprises await you. Eating olives means contentment and loyal friends. Taking them from a jar promises a merry gathering. Breaking a jar of olives warns of disappointment on the eve of a celebration.

You see a lot of onions. Your success will stir envy, but you will overcome it. Eating onions means you will overcome all resistance. Onions growing in a bed mean some rivalry, just enough to keep things interesting. Cooked onions promise calm and a small income. Cutting onions until your eyes water warns that rivals may get the upper hand.

You eat oranges. Worries lie ahead: someone close will need your care, and there will be discontent at work. Orange trees with ripe fruit promise health and well-being around you. If the oranges are juicy and tasty, the troubles will be lighter. Slipping on an orange peel warns of worries in the family.

You eat oysters. Don't let a thirst for pleasure and profit override your conscience. Seeing oysters promises a comfortable life and a big family. Selling oysters means you will be too pushy in chasing love or money.
You eat pancakes. Everything you take on now will go well. Making pancakes means you will be thrifty and good at running a home.

You eat peaches. Small disappointments are possible: work will give less than you expect, and planned trips may fall through. Peaches on leafy trees mean you will get what you want, but with effort. Dried peaches warn of people who may steal from you. For a young woman, picking juicy peaches promises a wealthy, wise husband. Green, hard peaches warn of coldness from relatives.

You eat peas. Good health and growing wealth lie ahead. Peas growing — lucky ventures. Planting peas — your hopes are well founded and will come true. Picking peas — you will enjoy the fruits of your work. Canned peas — your hopes will hang in doubt for a while, but luck will set them free. Dried peas — you are overloading yourself.

Pepper burns your tongue. Your love of gossip will cause trouble with people you know. Red peppers growing — a thrifty, independent partner. Heaps of pepper pods — you will firmly defend your rights. Grinding black pepper — beware of clever schemers. A pepper shaker on the table — sharp words and quarrels.

You eat pickles. Without energy and good judgment you may waste effort on worthless pursuits. Pickles promise trouble in love, but a win in the end. Craving pickles — rivals appear, so keep your private life private. Spoiled pickles — lovers’ quarrels.

You see rice. Success and warm friendships are on their way, and your work will bring a good harvest. Eating rice: happiness and comfort at home. Rice mixed with dirt: look after your health; you may be parted from friends. For a young woman, cooking rice means new duties that will make her happier.
You see salt. Discord and grumbling may start at home; be patient with those close to you. Salting meat: beware of debts. For a young woman, eating salt means jealousy and a rival.

You are eating soup. Good news and comfort await you. Watching others eat soup: promising acquaintances and a chance of marriage. For a young woman, making soup: a comfortable life. Eating creamy seafood soup: a quarrel followed by making up.
You see strawberries. You will get something you've long wished for, and things will go up. Eating strawberries means love that is returned. Selling them means a rich harvest and happiness.

You see sugar. At home you may grow too picky and jealous for no reason. Value what you have. Eating sugar means troubles that won't last and will end better than you expect. Spilled sugar means a small loss.

You brew tea. You may act carelessly and regret it later. Think before you act. Drinking tea with friends means usual fun will bore you and you'll want to help others. Tea leaves at the bottom mean trouble in love. Spilling tea means a household mess. Craving tea means unexpected guests.
You eat tomatoes. Good health and energy await you. Tomatoes growing in the garden mean joy in the family. For a young woman, ripe tomatoes promise a happy marriage.

You eat vegetables. Success may prove deceptive: check who you are dealing with. Wilted or rotten vegetables bring sadness and disappointment. For a young woman, cooking vegetables means losing interest in one admirer but later meeting a reliable, faithful partner.

You see fields of wheat. Your affairs will gain good prospects. Ripe wheat means a secure living and happy love. Grain in sacks points to victory soon and lasting feelings. Grain getting wet in the barn warns you to guard what you have earned from others. Climbing a hill by holding on to the stalks means great success in anything you choose.

You see bottles of whisky. You will watch over your affairs carefully and make them grow. Drinking whisky alone warns you not to put your own interests above your friends. Whisky seldom promises good: you will get what you want only after several disappointments.

You drink wine. Joy and new friendships await you. Breaking bottles of wine warns you not to lose all restraint in passion. Barrels of wine mean great plenty. Pouring wine from one vessel to another points to varied pleasures and interesting trips. Selling wine means well-paid work.
You see bats. A gloomy dream: worries and a run of bad luck; look after yourself and your family. A white bat is an especially troubling sign; avoid risks for a while and stay close to your family.
You see a bear. Fierce competition lies ahead in everything you take on. Killing a bear — you will free yourself from old entanglements. For a young woman — a rival or some misfortune.

You see a butterfly among flowers and grass. Prosperity and fine achievements. Butterflies fluttering about mean news from faraway friends. For a young woman, a butterfly promises a happy love that grows into a lifelong union.

You see a camel. You will have the patience and strength to get through even a very hard time. Owning a camel means wealth. A caravan of camels in the desert means help will come when hope seems almost gone, and you will recover against all odds.

You see a cat. Bad luck, unless you chase it out of sight. A cat attacking you means enemies will try to blacken your name. Driving it away means you will overcome big obstacles. A thin, dirty cat means worrying news about a friend, but all will be well. A meowing cat means a false friend is working against you behind your back. A cat scratching you means someone will try to take the profit you earned. A white cat means a tangle that only seems harmless.
You see a caterpillar. Hypocrites are near you; do not trust fine words. Setbacks in love or work are possible. You may be put in an awkward spot that brings little honour or gain.

You see a brood of chicks. You will have many worries, but some of them will turn to your advantage. Half-grown chickens — a lucky venture if you put real effort into it. Hens going to roost — rivals are plotting something. Eating chicken — selfishness may spoil your good name.
You see a cobweb. Insincere friends may cause you loss and upset. A firm, unyielding web means you will stand firm against envious people.
You see cows waiting to be milked. Your hopes and wishes will be generously fulfilled. Well-fed, calm cows — plenty at home. Take care of whatever feeds you.
You see crabs. You will have to untangle complicated matters, and you'll need all your good sense. For lovers the dream promises a long and tricky road to getting together.

You see a flock of cranes in the sky. Cranes flying south — a happy reunion with people far away and faithfulness in love. Cranes flying north — things will go slowly, and a letdown is possible. Cranes landing — something important is about to happen.
You hear a cricket. A cricket foretells sad news from far away. Seeing crickets — money troubles; plan your spending ahead.

You see a crocodile. Even your closest friends may deceive you, and rivals will lie in wait at every turn. Stepping on a crocodile's back — trouble that will take a long struggle to escape. Don't rush to share your secrets, even with friends.
You see a crow. A crow foretells bad luck and grief. Hearing crows caw — someone will talk you into a bad deal over property; don't give in. For a young man — beware of cunning temptations.
You see a deer. A good dream: true, deep friendships for the young, and a calm, steady life for families. If you kill a deer, enemies will hound you. Hunting deer warns that a project may fail.

A dog nuzzles up to you. Great gains and loyal friends. A vicious dog means enemies and trouble. A dog biting you warns of a quarrelsome partner in marriage or business. A friendly white dog promises success in work and love. A dog following you on a journey means steadfast friends and good fortune. A dog howling foretells a long separation from friends.
You see a dolphin. Not a very good dream: changes beyond your control are coming, such as a new boss. Get to know the new rules and the people in charge before you trust them.

You are riding a donkey. Journeys to distant lands and hard but exciting paths lie ahead. A donkey braying in your face warns of public rudeness. Falling off a donkey means setbacks and a lovers' quarrel. Being given or buying a donkey promises success and a happy marriage. A white donkey means lasting wealth and time for what you love.

You see a flock of white doves. Peaceful joys and happy changes ahead. Doves building a nest mean peace and harmony at home. A dove bringing a letter means good news from distant friends and lovers making up. The mournful cooing of a dove brings sadness and disappointment.
You see a dragon. You often let your feelings take over, and enemies may use that against you. The dream advises self-control: outbursts of anger now work against you.

You see wild ducks on clear water. Lucky journeys, perhaps even overseas. Ducks in flight promise a brighter future, sometimes a wedding and children. White ducks around the house mean plenty. Hunting ducks warns that plans at work may go awry.
You see a falcon. Your success will stir up envy and ill will. For a young woman, the dream warns that a rival may spread gossip about her.

Feathers are falling around you. Life's burdens will be light and easy to carry. An eagle feather means your hopes will come true. Chicken feathers mean small annoyances. Black feathers warn of disappointment in love.

You see fish in clear water. Fish in clear water mean the support of influential people. Catching fish while wading: wealth earned by your own work. Eating fish: a warm and lasting attachment. Dead fish: losses, so avoid risking money. Fishing and catching nothing: your efforts won't pay off yet.

You see a fox. Beware of envious 'friends': someone is quietly harming your good name. Chasing a fox: you are getting into dubious schemes and risky romances. Killing a fox: you will win every contest.

You see goats grazing near a farm. Fine weather and a good harvest: your wealth will steadily grow. A billy goat butts you: keep your secrets and plans away from rivals. Drinking goat's milk: a practical marriage that won't disappoint.

You see goldfish. Many lucky and pleasant adventures await you. For a young woman, goldfish promise a comfortable marriage to a pleasant person. If the fish are sick or still, expect a disappointment.

You see grasshoppers on green plants. Someone may be threatening your interests; stay on guard. Grasshoppers between you and the sun: you'll have an irritating problem to solve, but with care it will turn out in your favour. Pointing grasshoppers out to others: you talk too openly about private matters.

You see a hawk. Cunning people will try to trick you. Keep an eye out for schemes around you. Shooting a hawk means you will overcome obstacles after a long struggle. A dead hawk means your rivals will be defeated. Chasing a hawk away from chickens means rivals are close, but your care will bring luck at work.

You see a hornet. An old friendship may crack and money may slip away. Protect both. A young woman stung by a hornet or caught in a hornets' nest: envious people will try to blacken her name in front of her admirers.

You ride a horse. Prosperity and a life full of joy are waiting for you. A white horse: good luck and pleasant company. A horse throws you: a strong rival will appear. A runaway horse: someone else's folly will hurt you. Catching and saddling a horse: everything you do will go up.

You see a hyena. Setbacks and unpleasant company are ahead. Choose carefully who you deal with. For lovers, a hyena means frequent quarrels. A hyena attacks you: gossips will go after your reputation.
You see a kangaroo. You will outsmart a sly rival who wants to show you in a bad light. A kangaroo attacks you: guard your reputation. Overcoming a kangaroo: you will succeed despite obstacles.

You see kittens. Small annoyances will pester you. Do not let them pile up. Chasing away or getting rid of a kitten: you will deal with these worries. Snakes attacking kittens: rivals trying to harm you will harm themselves. A woman seeing a fluffy white kitten: someone will try to deceive her, but her good sense will protect her.

You see lambs playing in a green meadow. Pure friendships, joy and growing prosperity await you. Lambs nursing from their mothers mean a happy home and lovely children. Carrying a lamb in your arms means sweet cares for those you love. A lost lamb means someone follows your example, so mind your actions. Dogs or wolves attacking lambs mean innocent people will suffer from schemers. Lambs in rain or a snowstorm mean hopes that fall short.

A leopard attacks you. The future looks bright, but trusting the wrong people will bring trouble. Killing a leopard means winning in your affairs. A caged leopard means enemies will surround you but fail to harm you. A leopard running from you means you will overcome trouble in work or love by persistence. A leopard skin warns of a charming cheat.

You see a lion. A great force is driving you forward. Overpowering a lion means victory in any contest. If the lion overpowers you, enemies may get the upper hand. Caged lions mean success depends on handling opposition. Lion cubs mean new ventures that will succeed with proper care. Hearing a lion roar means an unexpected promotion. Riding a lion means courage and persistence in hardship. A lion snarling over you warns you to be careful on your way up.

You see a lizard. Enemies will try to attack you. Killing a lizard means you will win back a lost reputation or money. If it gets away, you will face annoying setbacks in love and work. For a woman scratched by a lizard, the dream foretells a hard stretch: arm yourself with patience.
You see a lynx. Enemies are quietly undermining your work and your peace at home. For a woman, the dream points to a sly rival in love. Killing the lynx means you will defeat your rival.
You see a magpie. Discontent and quarrels lie ahead. After this dream, watch your words and actions closely.

You see a mole. You have hidden ill-wishers, so keep an eye on the people around you. Catching a mole means you will overcome resistance and rise. Moles on the skin warn you to look after your health and avoid quarrels.

You see a monkey. Sly people will flatter you for their own gain, so don't trust sweet words. A dead monkey means your worst rivals will soon back off. Feeding a monkey warns of a flatterer who may betray you. For a young woman, the dream advises not to delay in love so as not to stir jealousy.
You see mosquitoes. Hidden rivals will pester you behind your back and test your patience. Killing mosquitoes means you will clear the obstacles and find comfort and peace at home.
You see a moth. Small worries will push you into hasty deals, so don't rush. The dream also warns of quarrels at home: be gentle with your family.
You see a mouse. A sly ill-wisher will appear and annoy you behind your back. Catching or chasing off a mouse means you will see through the tricks and get rid of small troubles.

You see a bird's nest. You will take up a venture that brings success. For a young woman, the dream foretells a move. An empty nest means sadness while a friend is away. A hen's nest promises joys at home and cheerful, obedient children. A nest with broken or rotten eggs foretells disappointment.

You see a panther and feel afraid. Agreements in love or work may suddenly fall through because of others' schemes. Killing or overpowering a panther promises joy and success in everything you start. A panther threatening you warns of letdowns at work and broken promises. Hearing its growl brings unwelcome news about income and discord among friends.

You hear parrots chattering. There will be a lot of idle talk and gossip around you, so don't take it seriously. Parrots sitting quietly promise a break in family arguments. Teaching a parrot to talk means trouble in your private affairs. For a young woman, owning a parrot warns that her partner may think her quarrelsome.

You see a peacock. Sorrows may hide behind glitter and luxury, so don't be dazzled by appearances. For a woman, owning peacocks warns she may misjudge someone's honesty. Hearing a peacock's harsh cry as it spreads its tail means a beautiful, charming person will cause you unease.
You see a fat, healthy pig. Your affairs will go sensibly and well. Pigs wallowing in mud — beware of bad company and dubious deals. For a young woman — a wealthy but jealous and greedy partner.

You see a polar bear. Trouble may come in a pleasant disguise: enemies will pretend to be friends. Rivals will try to take your place. A polar bear skin — you will successfully overcome any opposition.
You see puppies. You will help someone defenseless and find joy in it. Healthy, well-formed puppies — friendships grow stronger and fortune increases. Thin, dirty puppies — the opposite.

You see rabbits. Things will turn for the better, and your gains will please you more than before. White rabbits — faithfulness in love, whether married or single. Rabbits playing — children will bring you much joy.
You see a rabid dog. Enemies will viciously attack you and your friends. Killing the rabid dog means you will overcome bad talk and earn well.

You see rats. Beware of deceit and harm from neighbors; quarrels with companions are possible. Catching rats — you will rise above others’ meanness and beat your enemies fairly. Killing a rat — victory in any contest.
You see a raven. The dream foretells a turn for the worse and discord around you. For a young woman, the dream advises a closer look at her beloved: he may prove unfaithful.
You see a rhinoceros. A serious risk of loss lies ahead, along with worries you will keep to yourself. Killing a rhinoceros: you will bravely get past every obstacle.
You see a rooster. You will be very successful and become well known; just do not let it go to your head. Roosters fighting: arguments and rivals.
You see a salmon. Good luck and pleasant tasks will fill your time. For a young woman, eating salmon means marriage to a cheerful partner with means to live comfortably.
You see a scorpion. False friends will look for chances to undermine your well-being. Failing to kill the scorpion: an enemy may do you harm; stay alert.

You see sharks. You have powerful enemies; be careful. A shark chasing you: setbacks and low spirits; hold on. Sharks playing in clear water: amid your success, someone's jealousy is growing. A dead shark: reconciliation and a fresh rise.
You see snails crawling. The atmosphere around you is unhealthy; take care of yourself. Stepping on a snail: you will have to deal with unpleasant people.

You see sparrows. Love and comfort will surround you, and your kindness toward others' troubles will win you wide affection. Frightened or hurt sparrows: sadness; support those who are having a hard time.

You see a spider. Careful, steady work will bring you a good income. A spider spinning its web means peace and security at home. Killing one means a quarrel with your partner. A spider bite warns of disloyalty and rivals at work. Many spiders in webs around you mean luck, health and true friends.

You see a squirrel. Pleasant friends will visit soon, and your affairs will go up. Petting a squirrel means joy in the family. Killing one means you'll be seen as unfriendly. A dog chasing a squirrel means quarrels among friends.

You see a stallion. Wealth and a respected position are coming your way. Riding a fine stallion means a rapid rise, but don't let success go to your head. A wild, raging stallion warns that wealth may make you arrogant, and friends won't like it.
An insect stings you. This is a warning of trouble and sorrow. Stay alert. For a young woman, it advises not to trust too fast: too much trust may bring regret.
You see swallows. Peace and harmony will fill your home. A wounded swallow means sadness you can't avoid, but it won't last.

You see white swans on calm water. Good prospects and pleasant experiences await you. Swans in flight mean happy hopes will soon come true. A black swan means forbidden temptations. A dead swan means boredom and discontent.

You see a tick on your skin. Guard your health and your money, and don't waste your strength. Crushing a tick means treacherous enemies will annoy you. Ticks on livestock mean someone is dishonestly eyeing your property.

A tiger comes toward you. Enemies will pester you. Don't show weakness. Fighting off or killing a tiger means great success in everything. A tiger running away means you'll overcome resistance and rise high. A caged tiger means you'll outwit rivals. A tiger skin rug means luxury and ease.

You see a toad. This points to ill-fated adventures. Don't take needless risks. For a woman, it advises guarding her good name against gossip. Killing a toad means your judgment will be harshly criticized. Holding a toad means you may unwittingly let a friend down.

You see turkeys. Good income awaits you, and a rich harvest if you farm. Eating turkey means a joyful occasion is coming. Turkeys flying mean a quick rise from obscurity. Sick turkeys mean hardships that will hurt your pride.
You see a turtle. An unusual event will bring you joy and improve your affairs. Eating turtle soup means you may be drawn into a risky affair.
You see a viper. Trouble is gathering over you; be careful. A brightly coloured viper attacking you means opponents have joined forces and act behind your back.
You see a vulture. A scheming person wants to harm you; their plan will fail if the vulture is wounded or dead. For a woman, the dream points to gossip and talk; do not take it to heart.
You see wasps. Ill-wishers will speak spitefully behind your back. A wasp stinging you means you will face envy. Killing a wasp means you will stand up to your opponents and defend your rights.

You see a whale approaching a ship. You will have to choose between different duties, and your property may be at risk. If the whale is defeated, you will make the right choice and succeed. A whale overturning a ship points to a string of troubles.

You see a wolf. There is a dishonest person near you who may give away your secrets. Killing a wolf means you will defeat sly opponents. Hearing a wolf howl means rivals are secretly plotting against you.
You see a zebra. You will be drawn to changeable, short-lived ventures. A wild zebra in its homeland means you will chase a dream that will not bring the expected joy once it comes true.
You see an alligator. This is a warning dream: be careful in everything on your mind. Killing the alligator — you will overcome the danger, and the dream turns good.

You see an eagle soaring above you. You have lofty goals and will reach them, though only after a struggle. An eagle on a distant peak means fame and a high position. Eaglets in a nest mean meeting influential people and getting wise advice. Riding on an eagle means a long journey in search of knowledge and wealth.

You are riding an elephant. Solid wealth and honour; your word will carry weight at work and at home. Many elephants mean great prosperity. A single elephant means a modest but secure life. Feeding an elephant means your kindness will raise you in others' eyes.
You see an ostrich. You will quietly build up a fortune. Catching an ostrich means your means will let you travel a lot and learn new things. The dream also advises staying out of shady affairs.

You hear the muffled hoot of an owl. Look after your health and don't take needless risks: the dream asks for caution. Seeing an owl means someone is secretly speaking ill of you, so beware of rivals. A dead owl promises a narrow escape from serious trouble. The dream may bring worrying news about people far away.

You see a well-fed ox. You will become a noticeable, respected person in your circle. Fat oxen in a green pasture promise luck and a rise beyond your hopes. Lean oxen mean your means may shrink and friends drift away. Oxen yoked together promise a happy, comfortable marriage. Oxen drinking from a clear stream mean a long-held dream will come true. A dead ox foretells sadness.
You see ants. A day of small hassles and petty annoyances lies ahead. Do not waste your energy on trifles: most of the worries will pass on their own.

You see bedbugs. Expect lingering troubles and low energy; take care of your health. A swarm of bedbugs means a stretch of worry. Crushing them brings a scare that turns out to be groundless. Scalding them with boiling water means difficulties you will overcome. Little bugs everywhere point to annoying household hassles.

You see bees. Pleasant and profitable work lies ahead: your efforts will bring joy and income. For a boss, bees promise a loyal team; for a trader, growing sales; for parents, joy from their children. A bee sting means someone close may hurt or let you down.
Beetles are crawling on you. Expect small troubles and money running short. Killing a beetle is a good sign: you will be rid of small worries.

You see birds flying. Prosperity is coming: everything unpleasant will give way to a wave of good change. Birds with bright, beautiful feathers mean good luck, and for a woman a happy meeting with a reliable partner. A wounded bird means sorrow over loved ones. Catching a bird is not a bad sign. Talking birds mean you lack clarity in an important matter.
You see fleas. Someone close to you may scheme and provoke you; don't take the bait. For a woman, being bitten by fleas warns of gossip from false friends. Fleas on a partner point to his fickleness.
You see flies. Look after your health and stay alert: ill-wishers may be around you. Killing or driving away flies: your quick wits will help you win back a loved one's affection.

You see frogs in the grass. You'll have a calm, even-tempered friend who gives sound advice. Catching frogs: don't neglect your health. Frogs in a marsh: trouble you'll overcome with the help of kind people. Hearing frogs croak: a visit to friends that won't bring much.

You see geese swimming. Your wealth is slowly growing. Geese on the grass: sure success. Plucking geese: coming into property. Eating goose: someone may dispute what belongs to you. Dead geese: losses and annoyance.
You see seagulls. You'll manage to get along peacefully even with stubborn, tight-fisted people. Dead gulls: a long separation from friends.

You find lice on yourself. Worries and unease lie ahead, especially about your health. Lice on your body warn you to mind how you treat acquaintances. Catching lice tells you not to give in to gloomy thoughts and to look after your health. Lice on livestock mean losses on the farm.

You see a flock of sheep. Good times and shared prosperity await you. Shearing sheep: a profitable stretch. Thin, sick sheep: a promising plan may fall through. Eating mutton: someone's rudeness will hurt you.

You see snakes. Hard times and ill-wishers lie ahead; watch the people around you. Killing a snake: you will beat your enemies and seize your chance. A snake bites you: bad influences may harm your work. Walking over snakes: worry, and others trying to take your place beside your partner. For a woman, bitten by a dead snake: beware the spite of a false friend.
You see vermin crawling. Troubles and tiredness lie ahead; save your strength. If you manage to get rid of them, your affairs will go fairly well and the worry will pass.

You see worms. Shady people will weave petty intrigues against you. For a young woman, worms crawling on her point to being too down-to-earth; throwing them off means reaching for higher things. Using worms as bait means you will cleverly turn your opponents' plans to your advantage.

You see a bright, lush bouquet. A pleasant surprise from fate and cheerful gatherings with friends. A bouquet may promise an unexpected inheritance or gift. A withered bouquet means disappointment and fatigue; save your strength.

You are camping in a tent under the open sky. Expect changes in your affairs and get ready for a long, tiring trip. Seeing a campsite means friends will move away and your own prospects will dim for a while. For a young woman, being in a camp means her partner will wait long for her yes but will prove kind. A military camp warns against rushing into love.

A cave yawns before you in the moonlight. Doubts and obstacles from rivals lie ahead; save your strength and look after your health. Being inside a cave means change and a possible cooling with people dear to you. For a young woman, walking in a cave with a friend means do not trust a charming but unreliable person.

You pick chrysanthemums. Coloured chrysanthemums promise pleasant meetings; white ones bring sadness and confusion. A bouquet of chrysanthemums — love will be offered to you; don't turn it down out of empty pride. An avenue of white chrysanthemums — a quiet sorrow that will leave you wiser and stronger.

You see a comet in the sky. Unexpected trials await, but if you face them bravely you will rise high and become well known. For young people the dream foretells sadness and worries that will toughen their character.
You see a creek. New experiences and short trips await you. An overflowing creek — sharp but brief trouble. A dry creek — a letdown: what you wanted will go to someone else.
You stand in a meadow full of daisies. A sunny field of blooming daisies means happiness, health and prosperity. A bunch of daisies brings a touch of sadness. Daisies out of season warn of trouble.

You wander through a bleak, empty desert. A heavy dream: hard times, hardship and losses. For a young woman to be alone in a desert means she should guard her health and good name and act more carefully.

You see a green field. A green or ripe field promises great abundance and happiness. A freshly ploughed field: income will rise soon and you will earn respect. A field ready for sowing: your long efforts will soon pay off. A dry, harvested field: bleak prospects.

A muddy flood is carrying you away. Unsettled times are ahead: look after your health, be careful at work and gentle with your partner. If you reach dry ground, the troubles will pass and life will settle again.

You walk through a forest of tall trees. A stately forest in full leaf means prosperity and pleasures. Getting lost in a dense thicket: setbacks at work and family arguments. Feeling cold and hungry in the forest: a long trip to sort out an unpleasant matter. For creative people, the dream promises recognition.

You see a fountain sparkling in the sun. A clear, sparkling fountain means wealth, great joy and pleasant travels. A muddy fountain: insincere people around you and setbacks in love. A dry, broken fountain: the end of familiar pleasures.

You see a garden full of flowers and greenery. Peace of mind and comfort await you. Walking with your love through a blossoming garden: cloudless happiness and comfort. Seeing vegetable beds: chores and money worries.
You climb a hill. If you reach the top, success awaits you. Slipping back down: you will have to fight envy and other people's stubbornness.
You go hunting and find game. You will overcome obstacles and get what you want. Hunting and finding nothing: you are chasing the impossible, so pick a closer goal.

A hurricane is heading toward you. A tense time is ahead: you will have to fight hard to keep your affairs on track. A hurricane tears a house apart while you pull someone from the wreckage: big changes and moves, though peace will not come at once. Looking at the damage after a hurricane: trouble will pass close by but miss you.

You sail across a clear, calm lake. Good company, happiness and enough money will be yours. A rough, muddy lake means changes and regret over past extravagance. A muddy lake among bare rocks means letdowns in work and love. Your reflection in a clear lake means joys and loyal friends. Slimy creatures rising from the water warn you not to waste your strength and health on shady pleasures.

You walk across a well-kept lawn. Reasons for joy and great success are coming. A cheerful party on a lawn means fun and successful dealings. Waiting for a loved one on a green lawn means your dearest wishes will come true. Dead grass and a soggy lawn mean quarrels and partings. Snakes in the grass mean betrayal and spiteful hints.
You see a lighthouse through a storm. Troubles and sorrow will come but give way to good fortune and happiness. A lighthouse over a calm sea means quiet joys and kind friends.

You see a lily. Sadness and worry over loved ones' health may come, but the trial will make you wiser. Lilies blooming among rich leaves mean an early marriage, but also partings. For a young woman picking lilies, the dream promises joy mixed with sorrow. Withered lilies mean sadness is closer than you think. Breathing in the scent of lilies means sorrow will purify you and make you stronger.
You see a blooming meadow. Happy reunions and bright hopes for the future await you. The greener and brighter the meadow, the happier your coming days.

You climb a green mountain slope. You will quickly gain wealth and standing. A steep mountain whose top you can't reach warns of setbacks, so work on your weak points. Waking at a dangerous spot in the climb means things will take a sudden turn for the better. Getting tired and stopping means your success will be a little smaller than you hoped.

You see palm trees. Good hopes and true happiness await you. Walking down an avenue of palms promises a cozy home and a faithful partner. Withered palms warn that an unexpected sadness will disturb your peace.

You walk through a well-kept park. Pleasant leisure awaits you. Walking in the park with someone you love promises a happy, peaceful married life. A neglected park with no grass or leaves warns of unexpected setbacks.

You walk along a narrow rocky path, stumbling. Difficulties lie ahead that will call for patience. Looking for your path and not finding it means something you started may not be finished. Walking along a path lined with green grass and flowers means you will be freed from what weighed on your heart.

You look into a deep pit. You risk getting into a foolish venture and worry about love. Falling into a pit — a hard stretch and grief. Waking up as you start to fall — you will get out of trouble in fairly good shape. Climbing down on purpose — you will risk health and money for greater success.
You see a pond. Life will run calm and even, and luck will stay on your side. A muddy pond — quarrels at home.
You see poppies. Tempting pleasures and flattering offers lie ahead, but none of them is solid. Breathing in a poppy’s scent — someone will try to win you over with flattery; do not give in.
You stand at the edge of a precipice. Be careful: serious trouble may lie ahead. Falling over the edge — a hard stretch; take no needless risks and lean on those close to you.

You step into a puddle. There will be some annoyance, but later something good will come of it. Muddy water — troubles will hang around for a while. Getting your feet wet — today’s pleasure will cause harm later.

You see a rainbow. Unusual events lie ahead, and your affairs will take a very hopeful turn. For lovers, a rainbow promises a happy union. A rainbow hanging low over green trees — complete success in any undertaking.

You see a clear river. Joys will come soon, and prosperity will make good promises. A muddy or raging river: quarrels and jealousy. A flooded river cuts off your way: short-term trouble at work and fear of gossip. A dried-up river: take care of your health; a run of bad luck.

You walk along a road. A road lined with trees and flowers brings pleasant, unexpected luck. A rough, unknown road: a new venture will bring more trouble than gain. Walking with friends: a happy home and family. Losing your way: a mistake in a work decision.

You see stones. Many difficulties lie ahead. The road will be rough but passable. Walking among stones means a hard road for a while. Pebbles mean small annoyances. Throwing a stone means you'll have to scold someone.

You see a storm coming. A hard stretch is ahead: health worries, setbacks at work, time apart from friends. Save your strength. If the storm passes by, the trouble will be lighter than it seemed. A sudden squall means disappointment at work. A raging tempest means friends may grow distant for a while.
You walk through a swamp. Circumstances will work against you, and love may bring disappointment. A swamp with clear water and green plants means luck and unusual joys, though they won't come easily.

You find yourself in the path of a whirlwind. A change is coming that may bring losses; meet it prepared. For a young woman, being caught in a wind that tugs at her clothes points to a secret flirtation that could turn into gossip.

You see trees in fresh leaves. Your hopes and wishes will come true happily. Dead trees mean sadness and loss. Climbing a tree means a quick promotion. Cutting down or uprooting a tree means wasting your energy and money.
